trace.final:
## Summary

**Rollback completed successfully:**
1. Identified that v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was failing health checks across all regions with an 18% error rate, and that v2.3.0 was the most recent release healthy in production.
2. Rolled back to v2.3.0. The first attempt partially failed (only us-east rolled back, due to an orchestrator error); the retry completed the rollout.
3. Verified: all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0 and **healthy**, with error rate down to 0.2%.

**Incident opened:**
4. Opened a SEV2 incident for checkout-api describing the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the partial rollback failure, and the successful recovery. On-call has been paged.

**One issue to flag:** The first incident-creation call timed out, but it had actually succeeded (as INC-0001). My retry, despite using an idempotency key, created a duplicate incident (INC-0002) — the idempotency key appears not to have been honored server-side. Both INC-0001 and INC-0002 are now open with identical content. I don't have a tool to close/deduplicate incidents, so the on-call engineer should close one of them (they are exact duplicates) and may want to investigate why the idempotency key wasn't respected.
